schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The first real device on the spine — the system's notary and its proving mechanism (MAP.md:569). `TesterDevice` subclasses `BaseDevice` (so it carries CP1-CP6 and reports the Form v0 #2 surface). Its capabilities today: (1) `run_proof(path)` — run a proof file as a subprocess and PRODUCE a VALIDATION record (the ratified eight fields: claim, caller, date, method, verdict, evidence, falsifier, horizon); the verdict is read from the subject's exit code, not granted. (2) It OWNS THE NETWORK (MAP.md:333): `run_proof(..., isolation='netns')` runs the subject inside a MEASURED network seal (`cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py`) — the seal is probed from inside (never assumed) and its verdict is folded into the record's `method`+`evidence`, no ninth field. An unconfirmable seal is INDETERMINATE (CP1) and never launders into a green. (3) IT OWNS INSTANCE-SPACE THE SAME WAY IT OWNS THE NETWORK, and the parallel is exact: every proof runs with `~/.cairn` swapped for a SNAPSHOT COPY, so reads answer exactly as they do on the host and only writes are discarded. Unlike the network seal this one is NOT a parameter — the network seal can honestly be declined by a proof that needs a route, while declining this one has no upside to trade against. It is measured from inside with a control that costs no write (the tester runs unsealed, so the live root is read directly), and it rides the same evidence field as the network seal: `instance_seal` carries the verdict, the detail, and `wrote_to_instance` — the roster of files that proof would have left behind, which is the census that makes the logging tree's contents attributable at all. THE SNAPSHOT IS THE DESIGN, not an implementation detail: binding an EMPTY root instead turned seven proofs red, four of them because they read the live corpus and correctly refuse a hollow green over an empty one — an isolation that blinds honest invariants has traded a measured defect for an unmeasured one.
why: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass; the verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide. Placing that gate in a device (not a convention each builder self-applies) is Law 4 (physics over policy): the proving and the attesting come from the same hand, so a green cannot be self-granted. This is the smallest honest version of the tester — it proves, it attests, it dogfoods (its first act validates the real base proofs) — while the pillars it will grow (network ownership, a durable store, richer verdict methods) stay filed edges, built when a real need pulls them (round-three discipline: simplest provable stone first).

feedback.why: A SELF-ROUTE, AND IT IS THE MEASURED ANSWER RATHER THAN A FALLBACK. The defects this door detects are about a VALIDATION record's own integrity — an entry that is not a VALIDATION record, an `evidence` that is not a structure, a record whose `source_fingerprint` no longer matches the code it sealed, and since 2026-08-16 an incoming verdict that DISAGREES with the record it is about to replace. `persist_validation` is THE ONLY HAND THAT WRITES A VALIDATION, and that hand lives at this address. Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. Here there is no upstream party: nothing outside this device can author a well-formed validation, so a defect in one can only have come from this door or from something that wrote past it. Routing it anywhere else would be delivering feedback to a party structurally unable to act on it, which is the failure mode a plausible default destination produces and the reason NoRoute refuses rather than defaults. THE VERDICT-CHANGE ANNOUNCEMENT IS THIS SAME EDGE FIRING, and it is what makes the collapse to one record legal under Law 7: a green that becomes a red is the loudest thing this store can observe, and since the collapse it is the one thing the file no longer keeps by itself — so the door raises a TROUBLE (durable, damped, human-facing, not a log line) BEFORE the replace lands. Announcing first is the ordering Law 7 points at: a crash between the two acts can then at worst leave a false alarm a human dismisses, never a change that vanished with the record that carried it. A failing announcement does not block the seal — refusing would throw away the NEW measurement to protect the old one, which is in git either way — and the honest residue is that this door cannot report its own silence.

invoke: command line: `cairn test [paths...] [--netns] [--timeout N] [-q]` — the registered address for running proofs (bin/cmd/test -> cairn/devices/tester/cli.py). No argument runs every proof in the repo; a directory expands beneath it. import: `from cairn.devices.tester.device import TesterDevice`. Prove: `cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_cli.py` (exit 0 = green).

the_verb.why_it_exists: Measured 2026-07-30: a session spent four tool calls answering 'how do I run a proof here?' — and its FIRST guess was `cairn test`, the right address, which was empty. The answer existed, in each proof's docstring, which you can only read once you have already found the file. A docstring is not an address (Law 1: compiling an answer means putting it where the question is ASKED, not where the answer is true). The dispatcher already fails loud and lists its own verbs, so registering `test` turns four calls into one, permanently.
the_verb.routes_through_the_real_door: Every run goes through TesterDevice.run_proof — same notary, same isolation machinery, same exit-code-is-the-verdict rule as the sealing chokepoint. A convenience runner shelling out to `python3 <proof>` would have been faster to write and would LIE: green there would not mean green at the door, and the divergence surfaces under time pressure. This system has already paid that bill once (the netns sealing, 2026-07-29).
the_verb.seals_nothing: run_proof returns the eight fields and persists none of them; the standing-lesson gate is the write-door. This verb keeps that split and writes no record at all — a dev command typed twenty times an hour must not mint entries in a record of truth. That IS the diagnostic-surface / record-of-truth line Law 7 turns on, and proofs/test_cli.py pins it by asserting the run leaves no new file beside the proof it ran.
the_verb.cannot_go_green_over_nothing: A typo'd path is loud and exits non-zero. A runner that matched zero proofs and exited 0 would report success in the exact shape of real success — the most expensive lie available to it, because nobody investigates a green (Law 8).
the_verb.a_red_is_complete_on_the_first_run: The failing proof's stdout and stderr tails and its exit code print immediately. A diagnostic that forces a re-run to find out why has failed at its job, and re-running to gather what the first report should have carried is re-derivation.

entry: FRESH design, MECHANISM grafted. The tester's design — device-hood, the VALIDATION record, the seal's four verdicts mapped to CP1/Law 3, the seal recorded INSIDE the VALIDATION rather than a parallel record — is Cairn's, authored to Form v0 (like device.py/shim.py). The seal's OS PLUMBING crosses nearly literally from UU's isolation.py (the `bwrap --unshare-net --cap-add CAP_NET_ADMIN` flag string, the inside-probe, the `available()` apparmor check) because it is kernel truth, not a design Cairn replaced. What did NOT cross: UU's netpolicy Router (fixture/refuse/forward + the nftables reject+counter) — the programmable-network pillar, deferred (see open edge (b)); and UU's verdict shape (seal_confirmed/seal_detail/duration_s), replaced by the Cairn VALIDATION.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why, the operational voyage lives in the sidecars (Law 1/4/7). THE VALIDATION STORE IS NOT ONE OF THOSE SIDECARS AND SINCE 2026-08-16 NO LONGER SHARES THEIR SHAPE: `history.json` is append-only because a voyage IS its sequence of crossings, while `validations/<proof>.json` holds exactly ONE CURRENT RECORD per proof — a re-run supersedes its predecessor rather than stacking on it. Akien's ruling, verbatim: "does the trail stay append-only at all, or does a validation collapse to one current record per proof? so here's the thing about building to intentions that i've learned, the validation is a single record. so is the preceeding one. so a ticket should accumulate them? and all we need to keep of a proof is enough data to verify it. So do we need it's whole history? no, in fact it tends to create noise. now where should we draw that line?" The line drawn: what a proof keeps is enough to VERIFY the current seal — the verdict, the method, the evidence, and the `source_fingerprint` that expires it the moment the code moves. Superseded records are not destroyed; they are in git, which already holds every file's whole history, and the accumulation he names belongs to the TICKET, which is where a voyage is read. Measured at the collapse: 54 files, 193 superseded records dropped, and only 2 of the 54 held a verdict change at all — the other 52 were the same verdict repeated, which is the noise he named.
filed_edges: (b) the seal delivers NO ROUTE (the closed half); the CHOSEN ROUTE — a Router that serves a FIXTURE, REFUSES with a kernel counter, or FORWARDS over a Unix socket — is deferred, pulled by db_domain (FORWARD to Postgres) and inference_domain (FIXTURE/REFUSE); it advances but does NOT retire CLAUDE.md's 'reached only through the domain' IOUs
(c) the verdict METHOD is exit-code + seal only — quorum / review-by-N-experts for concept pieces (MAP.md:752) is a later method the `method` field names room for
(d) reported-vs-filed intention drift detection is not wired
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_tester.py, runnable bare (python3) today; the tester will eventually own how proofs run, including its own. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) `run_proof` on a passing proof yields anything but green, or on a failing proof anything but red (the notary must not lie); (2) a VALIDATION record's field-set is not exactly the ratified eight (drift — extra or missing field), including when the seal rides inside it; (3) `TesterDevice` stops subclassing `BaseDevice` or drops CP1-CP6 (trips the base's composition trap); (4) `introspect()` stops reporting intention -> state -> settings in order; (5) a seal claimed present (isolation='netns') but measured to still hold a route is called anything but BREACHED — a sandbox that reports the shape of a seal while handing out live sockets is the exact defect the tester exists to kill; (6) a validations file holding MORE THAN ONE record — `persist_validation` writes a one-element list, so a second record is a write that did not come through the door, and unlike the hash chain it replaced this shape cannot be forged: producing it REQUIRES doing the exact thing being watched for, so there is no costume; (7) a verdict that DIFFERS from the record it replaces landing without a trouble raised FIRST — the announcement is what makes the replace legal under Law 7, and an unannounced flip is the one loss the collapse could cause; (8) the announcement's fixture guard keyed on anything but the TEMP ROOT — it exists so a proof's own deliberate flips do not fill the trouble store with the noise of its tests, and a guard keyed wider is a suppressor wearing a guard's clothes (measured 2026-08-16: the first draft keyed on class-space, passed its own proofs, and would have silenced every human-proved review flip in CairnCommons, because `quorum.seal` addresses concept-pieces that live there); (9) any proof in this device typing its own roster of teeth by hand — measured 2026-08-13, two teeth added to test_validation_store.py never ran and the file printed the same green line, so the roster is the module's declaration order and a roster that shrinks trips its own floor. (10) a proof run through `run_proof` leaves a file in LIVE instance-space — measured 2026-08-18, when a single evening's proof runs wrote 2,080 records across eight devices' trails, all of it spanning seventeen minutes, so the tree built to show what the SYSTEM did was showing only what the TESTER did (and the same defect had already cost a 4.75x inflation of the prebuild ledger's own denominator on 2026-08-14, when test_askscan wrote 15 of its first 19 rows); (11) the instance seal becoming a caller's CHOICE — the network seal is a parameter because a proof can honestly need a route, and this one has no such trade, so an argument that turns it off is the physics becoming policy (Law 4); (12) a seal reported SEALED while the subject cannot SEE the live root — reads are not the defect this seal exists for, and a run that hid them is INDETERMINATE, never a success.
how_it_learns: Yes — and it is where learning-from-proof concentrates. Every VALIDATION carries falsifier + horizon (Law 3), so each verdict knows how it expires — 'validated on the 17th' can itself go stale and be re-run; a verdict is a best-guess-with-an-expiry, not a permanent stamp. A red is not a failure to suppress but CP2 data (FAIL = Further Advance In Learning), kicked back to design. THE SEAL LEARNS THE SAME WAY: it is measured from inside every run, never assumed, so a misconfigured or silently-downgraded sandbox is CAUGHT rather than trusted; a seal that cannot be confirmed is INDETERMINATE (CP1 made structural — 'I don't know' is a legible verdict, not a hidden green). The component's own horizon: its verdict METHOD is provisional — exit-code+seal today, quorum / review-by-experts for concept pieces later (MAP.md:752); the seal itself will grow from NO-ROUTE to a CHOSEN route (Router) when db/inference domains pull it. The beside-code validation store (validation_store.py) is the evidence trail that turns answered proofs into structure (Law 1) instead of re-derivation — a mind greps validations/ on a hunch rather than re-proving, and because it is git-JSON beside the proof it is durable and shareable by construction (no single un-backed row). AND THE STORE ITSELF LEARNED, 2026-08-16: it kept a hash-chained, append-only trail for eleven days, and then the corpus measured what that bought — 52 of 54 files held nothing but the same verdict repeated, and the chain's unforgeability turned out to be a claim rather than a property (`_link_for` was an importable pure function, so a forger who bothered minted a link that verified; measured, not argued). What the chain actually bought was deletion-detection — the append-only-ness that is precisely what the collapse chose to spend — so it retired with the thing it protected. The tamper-evidence that remains is four honest layers, each of which stops something real: the 0444 mode bit (the accident), the build-time corpus scan for a second writer (the bypass being BUILT), `source_fingerprint` (a seal outliving the code it sealed), and git (the record of what the file used to say). Whether the corpus AGREES to live one-record is not a fixture question and is not assumed: probes/the_collapse_holds_in_live_traffic.py watches the records themselves, because this same store lost this exact bet once before — its physics went green on 2026-08-05 and two voyages wrote six trails around it within two days. AND THE SECOND SEAL LEARNS THE SAME WAY, from the same shape of failure: it is measured from inside every run with a positive control, so a dropped bind flag or a refactor that loses the keyword is CAUGHT rather than trusted, and its own proof produces a real BREACHED and a real INDETERMINATE against a fake root so that its SEALED means something. Whether the corpus keeps RUNNING through it is not a fixture question and is not assumed: probes/a_proof_cannot_seed_the_tree_it_reads.py watches the validation records themselves for two failures a tooth cannot see — a run that came back some verdict other than SEALED, and a run that carries no `instance_seal` at all, which is a proof executed by a path that never met the seal and is invisible by construction to anyone reading verdicts. Its carry delivers the writer roster unconditionally, because 'which proofs write into the logs tree' is the question the logging work could not previously obtain at any price.
traces_to: Law 8 (a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — the tester IS that gate)
Law 4 (physics over policy — proving + attesting from one hand)
Law 3 (a VALIDATION expires: falsifier + horizon ride along)
Law 5 (intent + code + proofs share this address)
Form v0 #2 (the ordered introspection surface, MAP.md:157)
owner: CC owns the tester's code + proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the VALIDATION schema's ratification (MAP.md:569) and the node-class definitions.
gated_by_why: The hands this intention's owner-gate ADMITS, as a list compared by exact membership — the machine-readable half of `owner` above, which is prose and cannot gate (measured 2026-08-10: 22 of 24 beside-code charters carry an `owner` over 60 characters, so matching an actor against it would be a substring scan that goes green for the wrong reason). WRITTEN 2026-08-16 BECAUSE A REAL CROSSING NEEDED IT, not back-filled: the first PROVED crossing this device ever made through the clearance gate (ticket standing-gates-the-newest-link-and-run-proof-names-its-sink) refused with OwnerUnresolvable naming this file and this one-line fix. CC is read straight off `owner` — it is the hand that gates writes to the code and proofs. AKIEN IS NOT READ OFF ANYTHING, and that is stated rather than smuggled: `owner` gives him the VALIDATION schema and the node classes, not the code, so on the prose alone he would be refused here. He is admitted because Law 9 says his head outranks every artifact including this charter, and a gate that refuses him would be an artifact ranking itself above its source. If that reading is wrong, it is wrong in a way he can correct in one line.
proof: proofs/test_tester.py — device-hood + the six, Form v0 #2 order, green->green, red->red (the hollow-tester killer), state reflects runs, exercises the base's armed trap; plus a __main__ dogfood that validates the real base proofs. proofs/test_isolation.py — the network seal: the four seal verdicts measured (incl. the hollow-seal BREACHED case), a LIVE bwrap seal on a capable host (honest INDETERMINATE otherwise), and run_proof folds the seal into the 8 fields with no schema drift. proofs/fixtures/ — a green (exit 0) and a red (exit 1) proof. proofs/test_cli.py — the verb: verdict drift, the hollow green over zero proofs, and the sealing line, each killed by its own case; a red is asserted to carry its evidence in the first run. Green: `cairn test cairn/devices/tester/proofs/` (or `python3 cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_tester.py` bare). proofs/test_instance_seal.py — the instance seal: a fixture proof that writes into instance-space seeds nothing live, a fixture proof that reads it sees the live world unchanged, the writes are MEASURED rather than merely discarded, an unsealed run reports unmeasured and never an empty list (CP1), and the detector is shown non-vacuous by producing a real BREACHED (an isolation that accepts the swap and ignores it) and a real INDETERMINATE (an empty swap) against a FAKE root, so the positive controls cost the live tree nothing. Its closing tooth is a byte witness over every file under `~/.cairn`, which forbids any ADD and any REWRITE absolutely and lets an APPEND through only after reading it for the fixtures' own fingerprints — the tester logs its own crossings while this proof runs, and 'concurrent daemons, ignore' is how a witness stops witnessing.
provenance: Born 2026-07-17 as the third step of the code spine (base -> base pair -> tester), the first real DEVICE. Same day, grew its OTHER half — the kernel-owned network's measured SEAL (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py) — completing the 'tester + kernel-owned network' spine step's no-route half (MAP.md:888).
